original_statement: I can't download the audit trail behind a signature — one file that describes the whole thing, from where its inputs came from through to how it settled.
restatement: A member can export, for any intent in a room they hold, one audit file covering the intent's whole lifecycle — every signature and exactly what each committed to, where each input came from, and how it settled — that verifies itself, is deterministic, and can reveal no more than the exporter could already read: (s1) for an intent, the export is one canonical-CBOR file containing the effect and its re-derived materialization, every signature on the intent with its full signing payload (profile, schema-id, environment, account, slot, expiry) and committed provenance record, the parent-closed log entries those records name, and the driver's manifest with its disclosure rows; every provenance-named log position resolves inside the file, and every entry in the file is named by a provenance record or is an ancestor of one that is; (s2) a pure verifier given only the file re-derives the materialization from the effect, recomputes every signing payload and verifies each signature against it, recomputes every entry's content id and parent-closure, and checks each provenance record against the included entries; an untouched file is accepted and any single-byte change is refused with the first discrepancy named; (s3) the file's bytes are a pure function of the room's log and keys: reordering or duplicating the log it is built from yields the byte-identical file, exporting twice yields the same digest, and producing it writes nothing to any store; (s4) the names in both the canonical file and the readable report are exactly the accounts that contributed — no missing, extra, or swapped signer; (s5) the file contains only entries from membership epochs the exporter holds keys for; if the intent's lineage reaches an epoch the exporter cannot open, the export is refused with that reason and never silently truncated; (s6) when the intent was submitted or finalized, those entries are included and graded as external reads with their chain reference, and the verifier never reports them as verified against the chain; the file states the lifecycle stage reached, so an unsettled intent is labelled as such; (s7) the human-readable report is a pure function of the canonical file and carries its digest: rendering is deterministic, every fact in it traces to a field of the file, and the report is never authoritative — editing it changes nothing the verifier says; (s8) the intent card offers a Download audit trail action that saves both the canonical file and the readable report; an offscreen self-test clicks it, runs the standalone verifier on the saved file, and gets accepted.

When the intent was submitted or finalized, those entries are included and graded as external reads with their chain reference, and the verifier never reports them as verified against the chain; the file states the lifecycle stage reached, so an unsettled intent is labelled as such.

The intent card offers a Download audit trail action that saves both the canonical file and the readable report; an offscreen self-test clicks it, runs the standalone verifier on the saved file, and gets accepted.

acceptance_tests.proves: The stepper enumerates intent lifecycles — propose; k-of-n signatures interleaved with declines and room messages; an admit mid-intent; submit; final — and at every reachable state exports and checks both directions: every provenance-named log position resolves to an entry inside the file, and every entry in the file is named by some signature's provenance or is an ancestor of one that is. Catches an export of only the caller's own signature, a slice that drops ancestors, and padding with unrelated room messages (over-disclosure).
acceptance_tests.description: For an intent, the export is one canonical-CBOR file containing the effect and its re-derived materialization, every signature on the intent with its full signing payload (profile, schema-id, environment, account, slot, expiry) and committed provenance record, the parent-closed log entries those records name, and the driver's manifest with its disclosure rows; every provenance-named log position resolves inside the file, and every entry in the file is named by a provenance record or is an ancestor of one that is.

acceptance_tests.proves: From a valid file the stepper enumerates single-field mutations across every field class — effect, materialization, each signing-payload field, signature bytes, provenance class and position, entry content, a dropped entry, reordered entries, a signature swapped from another intent, an entry spliced from another room — and requires each to be refused with a named discrepancy while the unmutated file is accepted; the verifier runs with no log, keys, or network. Catches a refuse-everything verifier, one that skips a field class, and one that silently consults the local log.
acceptance_tests.description: A pure verifier given only the file re-derives the materialization from the effect, recomputes every signing payload and verifies each signature against it, recomputes every entry's content id and parent-closure, and checks each provenance record against the included entries; an untouched file is accepted and any single-byte change is refused with the first discrepancy named.

acceptance_tests.proves: Across randomized log supply orders and duplications the exported file is byte-identical, and a store snapshot taken before and after export is unchanged. Catches map-order or timestamp nondeterminism in the export and an implementation that caches a side-car audit file.
acceptance_tests.description: The file's bytes are a pure function of the room's log and keys: reordering or duplicating the log it is built from yields the byte-identical file, exporting twice yields the same digest, and producing it writes nothing to any store.

acceptance_tests.proves: The stepper enumerates every signer-to-approval assignment (by transposition from the identity) and requires the canonical file AND the rendered report to name exactly the accounts that contributed, covarying with the assignment. Catches a file or report that drops, invents, or swaps a signer. Amended 2026-09-23 by ADR-015: anonymous membership is retired, so there is no silent branch.
acceptance_tests.description: The names in both the canonical file and the readable report are exactly the accounts that contributed — no missing, extra, or swapped signer.

acceptance_tests.proves: The stepper enumerates joins, admits and re-keys crossed with the exporter's held epoch keys and the epochs the intent's lineage spans; at every state every entry in the file is from a readable epoch, the export is refused with an epoch reason when the lineage touches an unreadable epoch, and it succeeds otherwise. Catches a late joiner exporting pre-join lineage, silent truncation into a file that claims to be whole, and blanket refusal (a counterexample).
acceptance_tests.description: The file contains only entries from membership epochs the exporter holds keys for; if the intent's lineage reaches an epoch the exporter cannot open, the export is refused with that reason and never silently truncated.

acceptance_tests.proves: The stepper enumerates lifecycle stages — proposed, collecting, executable, submitted, final, declined — and at each requires the file's stage label to equal reduce(log)'s stage, submit/final entries to be present exactly when in the log and graded external-read with a chain reference, and the verifier's result never to grade them as proven. Catches an unsettled intent labelled as settled and a chain result dressed as cryptographically verified.
acceptance_tests.description: When the intent was submitted or finalized, those entries are included and graded as external reads with their chain reference, and the verifier never reports them as verified against the chain; the file states the lifecycle stage reached, so an unsettled intent is labelled as such.

acceptance_tests.proves: On randomized files the report renders identically twice, contains the file's digest, changes whenever any rendered field of the file is perturbed (so it is not a static template), and editing the report leaves the verifier's result unchanged; the renderer takes only the file. Catches a report that pulls live state or can drift from the file it claims to describe.
acceptance_tests.description: The human-readable report is a pure function of the canonical file and carries its digest: rendering is deterministic, every fact in it traces to a field of the file, and the report is never authoritative — editing it changes nothing the verifier says.

acceptance_tests.proves: An offscreen runner proposes an intent, collects approvals, clicks Download audit trail on the card, finds both files saved, runs the standalone verifier on the canonical file and gets accepted, and matches the report's digest to it. Catches an unwired button, a UI export that differs from the module's, and a report that doesn't match its file.
acceptance_tests.description: The intent card offers a Download audit trail action that saves both the canonical file and the readable report; an offscreen self-test clicks it, runs the standalone verifier on the saved file, and gets accepted.
